sumInsured: Not specified in provided extract (Base Sum Insured as per Policy Schedule)

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: The Recharge shall be available for same illness as well different illnesses.
great.explanation: Automatic recharge can be used for the same illness as well as different illnesses. This helps if you have repeat hospitalizations for the same condition in the same policy year.

great.name: Modern Treatments
great.quote: The Company will indemnify the Insured Person up to Base Sum Insured for expenses incurred ... for treatment taken through following advance technology methods: ... Robotic surgeries ... Stereotactic radio surgeries ... Immunotherapy- Monoclonal Antibody ...
great.explanation: Advanced technology treatments like robotic surgeries, stereotactic radio surgeries and immunotherapy (monoclonal antibody) are covered up to the Base Sum Insured. This reduces the risk of these newer treatments being denied or paid with small caps.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) ... shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are not covered for the first 36 months of continuous coverage. Claims for declared/known conditions will be payable only after this waiting period ends.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with the Company.
good.explanation: Listed specific illnesses/surgeries are not covered for the first 24 months of continuous coverage. This can delay coverage for common planned procedures in the initial years.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered in the first 30 days, except if the claim arises due to an accident. This means you should not expect coverage for non-accidental ailments immediately after buying the policy.

good.name: Room Rent
good.quote: If the Policy Schedule states 'Single Private Room' as eligible Room Category, it means the maximum eligible Room Category ... is limited to stay in a Single Private Room.
good.explanation: Room eligibility can be limited to a Single Private Room if your Policy Schedule states that category. Choosing a higher room category than eligible can increase out-of-pocket costs depending on how the insurer applies room-category rules.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: Benefit 6 : Domiciliary Hospitalization The Company will indemnify the Insured Person ... for the Medical Expenses incurred towards Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.explanation: Medical expenses for domiciliary hospitalization (treatment at home when it qualifies) are covered. This is useful when hospital admission is not possible or not advised, subject to policy conditions.

good.name: Restore Benefit
good.quote: The Company agrees to automatically make the re-instatement of up to the Base Sum Insured once in a policy year
good.explanation: Up to the Base Sum Insured can be reinstated automatically once in a policy year after it gets exhausted. This gives you an extra layer of coverage for additional hospitalizations in the same year.

good.name: Optional Cover
good.quote: If this Optional Cover is opted, then Policyholder is entitled for a discount of 15% on the Premium payable... If the Insured Person takes Medical Treatment in hospitals other than those listed in Annexure – IV ... shall bear a Co-Payment of 20% on each and every Claim
good.explanation: Opting for this cover gives a 15% premium discount but imposes a 20% co-pay on each and every claim if treatment is taken outside the hospitals listed in Annexure IV. This can materially increase your out-of-pocket costs if you use a non-listed hospital.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Any item or condition or treatment specified in List of Non-Medical Items (Annexure – II to Policy Terms & Conditions).
bad.reference: Clause 4.2(1) and Annexure II (List of Expenses Generally Excluded)
bad.explanation: Non-medical/consumable items listed in Annexure II are excluded from payment. This can add meaningful out-of-pocket costs during hospitalization (e.g., gloves, syringes, masks, etc.).

bad.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
bad.quote: Under Relevant Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses, for a period of 30 days immediately prior to the Insured Person's date of admission
bad.explanation: Pre-hospitalization medical expenses are covered only for 30 days before admission. Diagnostic tests and consultations done earlier than 30 days may not be reimbursed.

bad.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
bad.quote: Under Relevant Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses, for a period of 60 days immediately after the Insured Person's date of discharge
bad.explanation: Post-hospitalization medical expenses are covered only for 60 days after discharge. Follow-up medicines and tests beyond 60 days will typically be out of pocket.

bad.name: NCB
bad.quote: In the event of a Claim occurring during any Policy Year, the accrued No Claims Bonus will be reduced by 10% of the Base Sum Insured at the commencement of next Policy Year
bad.explanation: On a claim, the accrued No Claims Bonus reduces by 10% of the Base Sum Insured at the next policy year start. This means your accumulated increase in cover can shrink after a claim instead of staying intact.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: The Company will indemnify the Insured Person for Medical Expenses incurred in respect of the below mentioned Ailments / Procedures up to the amount specified against each and every Ailment /Procedure mentioned in the Policy Schedule ... (These conditions will apply only if specifically mentioned in the Policy Schedule)
bad.explanation: If your Policy Schedule specifies sub-limits for named ailments/procedures, payouts for those items are capped to the stated amounts. This can significantly reduce claim settlement for those treatments even when your Sum Insured is higher.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: The Co-payment, if and as specified in the Policy Schedule, shall be borne by the Policyholder / Insured Person on each Claim
bad.reference: Clause 3(g) – General Conditions Applicable To All Benefits And Optional Covers
bad.explanation: A co-pay can apply if it is mentioned in your Policy Schedule, and then you must bear that share on each and every claim. This is a red-flag cost-sharing clause, so you should check the schedule carefully before buying/renewing.

unclear.name: Cashless Network
unclear.quote: For an updated list of Network Providers ... the Insured Person may refer to the list of Network Providers available on the Company's website or at the call center.
unclear.explanation: The wording points you to the insurer’s website/call center for the current network hospital list but does not state the network size. Your cashless options will depend on the live network in your city at the time of treatment.
